title: Dealing with exam stress
titleChinese: 应对并克服考试压力的方法
paragraphs: How do you feel about exams? Is it the one thing you dread or an experience you relish because it's your time to shine? Every year, many young people sit exams and whether they love or loathe them, most of them will face some anxiety in the lead up to the big day.

If you're anxious about your exams, don't worry, you're not alone. It might seem like a stressful time when the pressure is on to pass that all-important test but take a deep breath and absorb some good advice from people who've been through the same experience as you.

Eating the right food can feed your brain and keep you alert. Nutritional therapist Kerry Torrens recommends making breakfast the most important meal of the day. She recommends eating energy-giving oats and eggs, which contain a nutrient called choline - thought to help cognitive performance and improve memory as we age. And don't forget to drink lots of water to keep you hydrated – some research even suggests students who take water into the exam hall may even improve their grades.

One thing I know I always need is a good night's sleep to help me work and think better the next day and that's what's recommended for anyone preparing for their exams. If you get good sleep your memory is better and that means you can retain the information you have revised. And it's good to wind down before bedtime too – no watching TV or chatting on social media!

A good way to reduce your stress is to write down your anxieties. This is something that Lisa Artis from the Sleep Council recommends because it can 'free your mind'. She also says sitting on your bed when you're cramming is not a good idea because then you associate that place with stress. Revising for exams can also sometimes seem relentless, so it's good to take breaks and reward yourself with a small treat, like a cake or a quick run around the block. There comes a point when your brain can't absorb any more information so you'll also need to know when to stop.

But if all this talk about revising and exams is still stressing you out, be assured that there are some people who will always be more on edge than you: your parents! They're there to support you but they'll be biting their fingernails, worrying about you and the final results. So maybe you need to give them some advice - chill, everything will be ok!

vocabulary.entry: dread [v.] /dred/ 害怕；担心 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: She dreads going to the dentist.
vocabulary.translation: 她害怕去看牙医。

vocabulary.entry: relish [v.] /ˈrelɪʃ/ 享受；喜爱 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: He relishes the challenge of a difficult task.
vocabulary.translation: 他享受艰巨任务的挑战。

vocabulary.entry: loathe [v.] /ləʊð/ 讨厌；厌恶 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: She loathes getting up early in winter.
vocabulary.translation: 她讨厌冬天早起。

vocabulary.entry: anxiety [n.] /æŋˈzaɪəti/ 焦虑；忧虑
vocabulary.example: Exam anxiety can affect performance.
vocabulary.translation: 考试焦虑会影响发挥。

vocabulary.entry: in the lead up to [phr.] /ɪn ðə liːd ʌp tuː/ 在……来临前
vocabulary.example: In the lead up to Christmas, everyone is busy shopping.
vocabulary.translation: 在圣诞节来临前，每个人都在忙着购物。

vocabulary.entry: nutritional therapist [n.] /njuːˈtrɪʃənəl ˈθerəpɪst/ 营养治疗师 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: A nutritional therapist helped her plan a healthier diet.
vocabulary.translation: 一位营养治疗师帮助她规划了更健康的饮食。

vocabulary.entry: oats [n. pl.] /əʊts/ 燕麦 (单数: oat)
vocabulary.example: Oats are a healthy breakfast choice.
vocabulary.translation: 燕麦是健康的早餐选择。

vocabulary.entry: choline [n.] /ˈkəʊliːn/ 胆碱 (生物化学词汇)
vocabulary.example: Choline is important for brain development.
vocabulary.translation: 胆碱对大脑发育很重要。

vocabulary.entry: cognitive performance [n.] /ˈkɒɡnətɪv pəˈfɔːməns/ 认知表现 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Sleep is essential for good cognitive performance.
vocabulary.translation: 睡眠对良好的认知表现至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: hydrated [adj.] /haɪˈdreɪtɪd/ 水分充足的
vocabulary.example: Drink water to stay hydrated during exercise.
vocabulary.translation: 运动期间喝水以保持水分充足。

vocabulary.entry: retain [v.] /rɪˈteɪn/ 记住；保留 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: It‘s difficult to retain new vocabulary without practice.
vocabulary.translation: 不练习很难记住新词汇。

vocabulary.entry: wind down [phr.] /waɪnd daʊn/ 放松；逐渐平静
vocabulary.example: Listening to music helps me wind down after work.
vocabulary.translation: 听音乐帮助我下班后放松。

vocabulary.entry: cram [v.] /kræm/ 临时死记硬背 (口语)
vocabulary.example: He stayed up all night cramming for the test.
vocabulary.translation: 他熬夜为考试临时抱佛脚。

vocabulary.entry: associate with [phr.] /əˈsəʊʃieɪt wɪð/ 把……和……联系起来
vocabulary.example: Many people associate the smell of coffee with mornings.
vocabulary.translation: 许多人把咖啡的味道和早晨联系在一起。

vocabulary.entry: relentless [adj.] /rɪˈlentləs/ 没完没了的；持续的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The relentless rain caused flooding.
vocabulary.translation: 连绵不断的雨导致了洪水。

vocabulary.entry: on edge [phr.] /ɒn edʒ/ 紧张不安的；焦虑的 (口语)
vocabulary.example: She‘s been on edge all day waiting for the results.
vocabulary.translation: 她一整天都紧张不安地等待结果。

vocabulary.entry: bite one’s fingernails [phr.] /baɪt wʌnz ˈfɪŋɡəneɪlz/ 紧张得咬指甲 (口语)
vocabulary.example: He bites his fingernails when he‘s nervous.
vocabulary.translation: 他紧张时会咬指甲。

vocabulary.entry: chill [v.] /tʃɪl/ 放松；冷静下来 (口语)
vocabulary.example: Chill out! Everything will be fine.
vocabulary.translation: 放轻松！一切都会好的。

vocabulary.entry: alert [adj.] /əˈlɜːt/ 警觉的；清醒的
vocabulary.example: A cup of tea in the morning keeps me alert.
vocabulary.translation: 早上一杯茶让我保持清醒。

vocabulary.entry: revise [v.] /rɪˈvaɪz/ 复习 (英式英语)
vocabulary.example: She‘s revising for her history exam.
vocabulary.translation: 她正在为历史考试复习。

vocabulary.entry: treat [n.] /triːt/ 小奖励；小零食
vocabulary.example: She bought herself a chocolate bar as a treat.
vocabulary.translation: 她给自己买了一块巧克力作为奖励。

vocabulary.entry: absorb [v.] /əbˈzɔːb/ 吸收（信息）；理解
vocabulary.example: It’s hard to absorb so much information at once.
vocabulary.translation: 一次吸收这么多信息很难。

sentences.english: How do you feel about exams?
sentences.chinese: 你怎么看待考试这件事？

sentences.english: Is it the one thing you dread or an experience you relish because it's your time to shine?
sentences.chinese: 它是你最害怕的事情，还是你乐于享受的经历——因为这是你大放异彩的时刻？

sentences.english: Every year, many young people sit exams and whether they love or loathe them, most of them will face some anxiety in the lead up to the big day.
sentences.chinese: 每年都有许多年轻人参加考试，无论他们喜欢还是讨厌考试，他们中的大多数人在考试来临前都会感到些许焦虑。

sentences.english: If you're anxious about your exams, don't worry, you're not alone.
sentences.chinese: 如果你对考试感到焦虑，别担心，不止你一个人这样。

sentences.english: It might seem like a stressful time when the pressure is on to pass that all-important test but take a deep breath and absorb some good advice from people who've been through the same experience as you.
sentences.chinese: 要通过那场至关重要的考试，压力确实很大，这段时间可能会让人倍感紧张，但深呼吸，听听那些和你有过同样经历的人的实用建议吧。

sentences.english: Eating the right food can feed your brain and keep you alert.
sentences.chinese: 吃合适的食物能为大脑补充能量，让你保持清醒。

sentences.english: Nutritional therapist Kerry Torrens recommends making breakfast the most important meal of the day.
sentences.chinese: 营养治疗师凯瑞·托伦斯建议让早餐为一天中最重要的一餐。

sentences.english: She recommends eating energy-giving oats and eggs, which contain a nutrient called choline - thought to help cognitive performance and improve memory as we age.
sentences.chinese: 她推荐食用能提供能量的燕麦和鸡蛋，它们含有一种名为胆碱的营养素——这种物质被认为有助于提升认知能力，还能随着年龄增长改善记忆力。

sentences.english: And don't forget to drink lots of water to keep you hydrated – some research even suggests students who take water into the exam hall may even improve their grades.
sentences.chinese: 另外别忘了多喝水，保持身体水分充足——有研究甚至表明，带水进考场的学生，成绩可能会更好。

sentences.english: One thing I know I always need is a good night's sleep to help me work and think better the next day and that's what's recommended for anyone preparing for their exams.
sentences.chinese: 我一直都知道，睡个好觉可以让我第二天更好地工作和思考，这也是给所有备考者的建议。

sentences.english: If you get good sleep your memory is better and that means you can retain the information you have revised.
sentences.chinese: 如果你休息的好，你的记忆力会更好，这意味着你能记住复习过的内容。

sentences.english: And it's good to wind down before bedtime too – no watching TV or chatting on social media!
sentences.chinese: 睡前放松也很重要——别再看电视或再社交媒体上聊天了！

sentences.english: A good way to reduce your stress is to write down your anxieties.
sentences.chinese: 有一个减轻压力的好方法，那就是把你的焦虑写下来。

sentences.english: This is something that Lisa Artis from the Sleep Council recommends because it can 'free your mind'.
sentences.chinese: 这是睡眠委员会的莉萨·阿蒂斯推荐的方法，因为它能“解放你的大脑”。

sentences.english: She also says sitting on your bed when you're cramming is not a good idea because then you associate that place with stress.
sentences.chinese: 她还说，临阵磨枪时坐在床上不是个好主意，因为这样会让你把床这个地方和压力联系起来。

sentences.english: Revising for exams can also sometimes seem relentless, so it's good to take breaks and reward yourself with a small treat, like a cake or a quick run around the block.
sentences.chinese: 备考复习有时也会让人觉得没完没了，所以适当休息、给自己一点小奖励是很有必要的，比如一块蛋糕，或者绕着街区快速跑一圈。

sentences.english: There comes a point when your brain can't absorb any more information so you'll also need to know when to stop.
sentences.chinese: 当你的大脑再也吸收不了更多信息时，你也需要知道该何时停下。

sentences.english: But if all this talk about revising and exams is still stressing you out, be assured that there are some people who will always be more on edge than you: your parents!
sentences.chinese: 但如果这些关于复习和考试的讨论，还是让你感到压力山大，那请放心，总有一些人会比你更紧张：那就是你的父母！

sentences.english: They're there to support you but they'll be biting their fingernails, worrying about you and the final results.
sentences.chinese: 他们会在你身边支持你，但也会紧张得坐立不安，为你和最终的成绩担心。

sentences.english: So maybe you need to give them some advice - chill, everything will be ok!
sentences.chinese: 所以或许你该给他们提提建议——放轻松，一切都会好的！
